title: B2 · Upper Intermediate
description: Argue clearly, understand complex texts and fast, connected speech with multiple speakers, and express nuanced opinions.

objectives.can_do: I can structure a clear argument using discourse markers.
objectives.title: Linking ideas: contrast and concession

activities.instruction: Write a short paragraph arguing for or against remote work, using at least three discourse markers.
activities.target: Although ... / However ... / On the other hand ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, name three discourse markers for contrast.
activities.target: however / although / on the other hand

activities.instruction: Argue for or against a topic you have not discussed in this unit.
activities.target: Although ... / Nevertheless ... / On the other hand ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can structure a clear argument using discourse markers.

activities.instruction: On your own, write a short paragraph arguing for or against remote work using three discourse markers.
activities.target: Although ... / However ... / On the other hand ...

checks.prompt: Which discourse marker introduces a contrast?

options: Although it rained, we went out.
Although it rained, but we went out.
Although it rained, however we went out.

objectives.can_do: I can express cause and consequence precisely.
objectives.title: Cause and consequence

activities.instruction: Explain one consequence of climate change using 'as a result' and 'owing to'.
activities.target: Owing to ... / As a result ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two phrases that introduce a consequence.
activities.target: as a result / consequently / owing to

activities.instruction: Explain a consequence of a topic you have not discussed in this unit.
activities.target: Owing to ... / As a result ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can express cause and consequence precisely.

activities.instruction: On your own, explain one consequence of climate change using 'as a result' and 'owing to'.
activities.target: Owing to ... / As a result ...

options: The match was cancelled owing to the rain.
The match was cancelled owing the rain.
The match was cancelled owing to raining.

objectives.can_do: I can talk about hypothetical situations using the second and third conditional.
objectives.title: Second and third conditionals

activities.instruction: Say what you would have done differently last year.
activities.target: If I had ... I would have ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say how to form the third conditional.
activities.target: if + past perfect / would have + past participle

activities.instruction: Say what a friend would have done differently last year, not about you.
activities.target: If he/she had ... he/she would have ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can talk about hypothetical situations using the second and third conditional.

activities.instruction: On your own, say what you would have done differently last year.
activities.target: If I had ... I would have ...

options: If I had studied, I would have passed.
If I studied, I would have passed.
If I had studied, I would passed.
If I had more time, I would travel more.
If I have more time, I would travel more.
If I had more time, I will travel more.

objectives.can_do: I can report what others said accurately using reported speech.
objectives.title: Reported speech and reporting verbs

activities.instruction: Report what a friend told you last week about their job.
activities.target: He told me that ... / She claimed that ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say how tenses change in reported speech.
activities.target: present → past / will → would

activities.instruction: Report what a colleague said, not a friend.
activities.target: He/She said that ... / He/She admitted that ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can report what others said accurately using reported speech.

activities.instruction: On your own, report what a friend told you last week about their job.
activities.target: He told me that ... / She claimed that ...

checks.prompt: Choose the correct reported sentence for 'I am tired' (he said):
Which reporting verb means 'decir que algo es verdad'?
Read: 'She claimed she had finished the report.' According to her, who finished it?

objectives.can_do: I can follow a structured argument and identify the main points.
objectives.title: Listening: following an argument

activities.instruction: Listen to a short argument and identify the main point and one supporting reason.
activities.target: The main point is ... / One reason is ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two words that signal a reason or a contrast.
activities.target: because / however / therefore

activities.instruction: Summarise an argument you heard outside this lesson.
activities.target: The speaker argued that ... because ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can follow a structured argument and identify the main points.

activities.instruction: On your own, listen and identify the main point and one supporting reason.
activities.target: The main point is ... / One reason is ...

checks.prompt: You hear: 'Remote work saves time; however, it can be isolating.' What is the speaker's second point?
You hear an argument with three supporting points. What is the speaker trying to do?

objectives.can_do: I can follow a conversation between several speakers speaking at natural speed.
objectives.title: Multiple speakers and fast speech

activities.instruction: Listen to a three-speaker conversation and identify who changed the plan.
activities.target: The woman changed the plan because ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say what 'dunno' and 'gotta' mean.
activities.target: dunno = don't know / gotta = got to

activities.instruction: Explain a reduced form you heard in a real conversation.
activities.target: kinda / wanna / gonna

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can follow a conversation between several speakers at natural speed.

activities.instruction: On your own, listen to a fast conversation and identify who changed the plan.
activities.target: The woman changed the plan because ...

checks.prompt: You hear three people planning a meeting. What do they finally agree?

objectives.can_do: I can understand connected speech and reduced forms in fast speech.
objectives.title: Connected speech and reduced forms

activities.instruction: Listen to fast connected speech and write the full forms.
activities.target: gonna → going to / wanna → want to

activities.instruction: Without looking, write the full forms of 'gonna', 'wanna' and 'gotta'.
activities.target: going to / want to / got to

activities.instruction: Explain a reduced form you heard in a conversation you have not studied.
activities.target: kinda / lemme / gimme

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can understand connected speech and reduced forms in fast speech.

activities.instruction: On your own, listen to fast connected speech and write the full forms.
activities.target: gonna → going to / wanna → want to

checks.prompt: You hear: 'I dunno what you mean.' What does 'dunno' mean?

objectives.can_do: I can infer a speaker's attitude and intention from tone and context.
objectives.title: Inference: attitude and intention

activities.instruction: Listen and infer whether the speaker is being sincere or ironic.
activities.target: The speaker is being ironic because ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two signals of irony in speech.
activities.target: tone of voice / contrast with the words

activities.instruction: Infer a speaker's attitude from a sentence you have not heard before.
activities.target: The speaker is ... because ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can infer a speaker's attitude and intention from tone and context.

activities.instruction: On your own, listen and infer whether the speaker is sincere or ironic.
activities.target: The speaker is being ironic because ...

checks.prompt: You hear: 'Oh great, another meeting.' What is the speaker's attitude?
Read: 'Well, that went brilliantly,' she said, rolling her eyes. What does she really mean?

objectives.can_do: I can recognise formal and informal register in speech and writing.
objectives.title: Register: formal vs informal

activities.instruction: Rewrite an informal message as a formal email.
activities.target: I am writing to ... / I would be grateful if ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two features of formal writing.
activities.target: no contractions / polite formulas

activities.instruction: Rewrite a formal sentence in an informal register.
activities.target: formal → informal register

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can recognise formal and informal register in speech and writing.

activities.instruction: On your own, rewrite an informal message as a formal email.
activities.target: I am writing to ... / I would be grateful if ...

checks.prompt: Which phrase is the most formal?
options: I would be grateful if you could reply.

objectives.can_do: I can use modal verbs to speculate about what I hear.
objectives.title: Speculation with modals

activities.instruction: Speculate about what happened in a situation the tutor describes.
activities.target: It must have ... / It might have ... / It can't have ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two modals for strong and weak speculation.
activities.target: must have = strong / might have = weak

activities.instruction: Speculate about a situation you have not discussed in this unit.
activities.target: It could be ... / It can't have ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can use modal verbs to speculate about what I hear.

activities.instruction: On your own, speculate about what happened in the situation the tutor describes.
activities.target: It must have ... / It might have ... / It can't have ...

objectives.can_do: I can present my opinion and respond to a colleague in a discussion.
objectives.title: Discussion and response

activities.instruction: Give your opinion on a proposal and respond to the tutor's different point of view.
activities.target: In my view ... / I see your point, but ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two phrases that respond politely to an opinion.
activities.target: I see your point, but / That is a fair point

activities.instruction: Discuss a topic you have not discussed in this unit and respond to a different opinion.
activities.target: In my view ... / I see your point, but ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can present my opinion and respond to a colleague in a discussion.

activities.instruction: On your own, give your opinion on a proposal and respond to a different point of view.
activities.target: In my view ... / I see your point, but ...

checks.prompt: Which phrase responds politely to an opinion?

objectives.can_do: I can summarise a discussion in writing.
objectives.title: Summarising a discussion

activities.instruction: Write a short neutral summary of a discussion you have just had.
activities.target: In brief ... / Overall, the discussion was about ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two phrases that introduce a summary.
activities.target: in brief / overall / in conclusion

activities.instruction: Summarise a discussion you did not take part in.
activities.target: In brief ... / Overall, ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can summarise a discussion in writing.

activities.instruction: On your own, write a short neutral summary of a discussion.
activities.target: In brief ... / Overall, ...

objectives.can_do: I can argue a point, follow fast conversation and infer attitude and register.
objectives.title: Conversación final B2
concepts: review: argumentation, fast speech, inference, register

activities.instruction: Argue a point of view with the tutor and respond to a counter-argument.
activities.target: B2 level conversation

activities.instruction: Without looking, list three things you can now do at B2 level.
activities.target: argue clearly / follow fast speech / infer attitude

activities.instruction: Argue a point about a completely new topic using B2 language.
activities.target: B2 level conversation in a new context

options: If I had studied harder, I would be working there now.
If I studied harder, I would be worked there now.
If I had studied harder, I would worked there now.

checks.prompt: Read: 'He was hardly overjoyed by the news.' How did he feel?
Listen: 'I dunno what you mean.' What does 'dunno' mean?
Listen: 'That said, we should consider the risks before deciding.' What does 'that said' introduce?
